title: Magician: Apprentice
author: Feist, Raymond E.
review: 3.5/5 solid intro to fantasy book, at times a bit simple and straightforward but the driving central conflict of the series is intriguing and I will definitely read book 2 (which is basically the second half of a larger book anyway). Sometimes skips over some things that don't feel as earned and it does lull a bit and feel a little aimless at times. I'm actually more excited for the Empire series with Wurts and Feist and I think this will give good context for that, the antagonist faction is very mysterious and interesting and I want to learn more, so it did its job there at least for setting up the larger series.

Arutha shook his head, watching men who had tried to kill one another working side by side as if it were the most natural thing in the world, then saluting one another. “Father used to say that, among man’s strange undertakings, war stood clearly forth as the strangest.”
